name: Admix
tagline: Multi-model AI chat that compares answers side by side across providers

pricing.notes: Official site lists Admix plans starting at $10/month; the Starter plan is $10/month.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 4,000 credits/month; 350+ models; 100 cross-chat memories; per-model memory.

pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (-20%); paid plans begin with a $1.99 7-day trial that auto-renews
pricing.hiddenCosts: Credits are model-dependent and multi-model/parallel comparisons consume multiple allocations; the paid trial auto-renews.

verdictSummary: A local chat UI with side-by-side replies is a weekend project when it calls OpenRouter, but Admix's value depends on access to many hosted models, a current catalog, provider routing, and a maintained account and billing layer. You can reproduce the comparison workflow. You cannot reproduce the model access and service layer for a flat $10 subscription.
coreLoopDIY: Send one prompt to selected models through OpenRouter, stream the replies into a side-by-side grid, and save the thread locally.
requirements: Provider and model IDs to compare
whatYouLose: Admix's bundled access to many providers under one subscription
A maintained model catalog and provider routing
Built-in image, search, and document workflows
Usage limits, billing, and support handled for you
moatNotes: bundled model access, catalog upkeep, and billing under one subscription
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay for one bill and one interface instead of managing several provider accounts, API keys, model IDs, and usage limits. The comparison grid is easy to copy; keeping model access and the account, billing, and storage layer working is the service.

priorArt.name: Open WebUI
priorArt.desc: Open-source self-hosted chat interface for local and hosted models.

priorArt.name: LibreChat
priorArt.desc: Open-source multi-model AI chat platform for self-hosting API-based assistants.

alternatives.name: Big-AGI
alternatives.desc: One prompt fans out across models and Beam can merge the answers; free software, paid API keys if you chase frontier models.

facts.install: Use the hosted web app with your API keys, or self-host with Docker/Vercel
facts.engines: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Azure, Bedrock, DeepSeek, Groq, Mistral, OpenRouter, Perplexity, Together, xAI, Ollama, LocalAI, LM Studio and OpenAI-compatible endpoints
facts.dataFormat: The open app stores chats and settings locally in the browser by default; hosted Pro adds synced cloud storage, and model requests go to whichever provider the user configures
facts.gapVsPaid: It can fan one prompt across models, but you must provision and bill each provider separately and its interface is less focused on clean answer comparison than Admix.
facts.setupBlocker: The free hosted app is immediate, but it does not include model usage: the user must bring provider API keys and understand provider billing

alternatives.name: ChatALL
alternatives.desc: The exact compare-everyone desktop app; use API-backed bots, because scraped web connectors break whenever vendors sneeze.

facts.install: Download the Windows installer, macOS DMG/Homebrew package, or Linux DEB/AppImage from GitHub Releases
facts.engines: Runs many providers concurrently, including API-backed OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Groq, Cohere, xAI and web-connected bots; each bot needs its own account or token
facts.dataFormat: Chat history, settings and login data stay in the local application profile; anonymous usage telemetry excludes prompt and response contents
facts.gapVsPaid: It is the closest functional match, but its web-account connectors are brittle and every provider still needs a separate working login or API credential.
facts.setupBlocker: You must bring working accounts or API tokens, and its reverse-engineered web connectors frequently break when vendors change their sites

alternatives.name: Cherry Studio
alternatives.desc: Same prompt, several models, side by side; bring API keys or make local models do the arguing.

alternatives.name: Open WebUI
alternatives.desc: Run several models in parallel columns and merge the result; free to run, source-available rather than open source.

facts.install: Run the official Docker image, install the Python package, or deploy with Kubernetes
facts.engines: Ollama and any OpenAI-compatible API, including LM Studio, vLLM, Groq, Mistral and OpenRouter; additional speech, image and search providers
facts.dataFormat: By default, chats and account data live in a local SQLite webui.db, uploads in a data/uploads directory and embeddings in the configured vector store; PostgreSQL and object storage are optional
facts.gapVsPaid: Parallel chats work, but the self-hosted interface is less focused on clean side-by-side evaluation and still leaves provider setup and billing to you.
facts.setupBlocker: A non-expert must install Docker or a compatible Python environment, mount persistent storage correctly, and separately provide Ollama or an API endpoint

alternatives.name: Cherry Studio
alternatives.desc: A desktop model cockpit with parallel answers, files, agents, and rather more settings than restraint.

facts.install: Download the signed desktop installer for macOS, Windows or Linux
facts.engines: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and many other cloud APIs; Claude, Perplexity and Poe web integrations; local models through Ollama or LM Studio; OpenAI-compatible endpoints
facts.dataFormat: Chats, assistants and settings are stored in the desktop app's local profile; optional WebDAV backup/sync and cloud model calls copy relevant content to those services
facts.gapVsPaid: Parallel answers work, but you must bring and manage every model endpoint yourself rather than getting Admix's focused, unified comparison service.
facts.setupBlocker: The app installs cleanly, but the first useful chat requires an API key or a separately installed local model server

rejectedAlternatives.name: Msty
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The desktop core is $0, but the terms limit it to private non-commercial use; paid work needs a license.

rejectedAlternatives.name: LibreChat
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A polished multi-provider chat, but it does not send one prompt to several models side by side.

notes: The interface is easy to reproduce; the useful question is whether the API bill and missing provider features still work for you.
prompt:
Build me a local multi-model comparison chat to replace Admix. Requirements:

- Node 22 + Express + better-sqlite3, a server-rendered shell with a little vanilla
  JS for streaming; no frontend framework, no build step.
- One OpenRouter key in .env, kept server-side; the server proxies all model calls.
- A model picker fed from OpenRouter's /models endpoint; select up to four models.
- One prompt fans out to the selected models and streams each reply into a
  side-by-side grid with model name, elapsed time, and token usage when reported;
  a failed model shows its error in its own column without killing the others.
- Markdown rendering with fenced code blocks and a copy button per reply.
- Threads, prompts, model ids, replies, and timestamps in SQLite; full-text search
  across saved threads; export a thread as Markdown.
- A running cost estimate per thread from OpenRouter's usage and pricing fields.
- Binds to localhost only. No accounts, no telemetry; prompts and replies leave the
  machine only for OpenRouter, and the README says so.
- Out of scope: auth, billing, mobile apps, image generation, hosted sync, and
  provider-specific tools like web search or file upload.
- README: setup, .env.example, and how to add a model id by hand if the catalog
  fetch fails.
